questions.q: If $A = \left[$\begin{cases}\dfrac{1}{5} & \dfrac{2}{5} \\ \dfrac{- 2}{5} & \dfrac{1}{5}\end{cases}$\right], B = \left[$\begin{cases}1 & 0 \\ i & 1\end{cases}$\right], i = \sqrt{- 1}$, and $Q = A^{T}BA$, then the inverse of the matrix $AQ^{2021}A^{T}$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
{AA}^{⊤} = \left[$\begin{cases}\dfrac{1}{5} & \dfrac{2}{5} \\ \dfrac{- 2}{5} & \dfrac{1}{5}\end{cases}$\right]\left[$\begin{cases}\dfrac{1}{5} & \dfrac{- 2}{5} \\ \dfrac{2}{5} & \dfrac{1}{5}\end{cases}$\right] = \left[$\begin{cases}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}$\right] = I$

$Q = A^{⊤}BA$

$⇒ Q^{2} = \left(A^{⊤}BA\right) \left($A^{⊤}BA\right)$

$= A^{⊤}B\left($AA^{⊤}\right)BA$

$= A^{⊤}B\left($I\right)BA$

$= A^{⊤}B^{2}A$

$⇒ Q^{3} = A^{⊤}B^{3}A$

$⇒ Q^{2021} = A^{T}B^{2021}A$

Now let $P = {AQ}^{2021}A^{T}$

$P = $A\left($A^{⊤}B^{2021}A\right)A^{⊤}$

given $AA^{⊤} = I$

$P = B^{2021}$

$B^{2} = $\left[$\begin{cases}1 & 0 \\ i & 1\end{cases}$]\left[$\begin{cases}1 & 0 \\ i & 1\end{cases}$\right] = \left[$\begin{cases}1 & 0 \\ 2i & 1\end{cases}$\right]$

$B^{3} = \left[$\begin{cases}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{cases}$\right]\left[$\begin{cases}1 & 0 \\ i & 1\end{cases}$\right] = \left[$\begin{cases}1 & 0 \\ 3i & 1\end{cases}$\right]$

$B^{2021} = \left[$\begin{cases}1 & 0 \\ 2021i & 1\end{cases}$\right]$

inverse of $P = \left(P^{- 1}\right) = \left(B^{2021}\right)- 1 = \left[$\begin{cases}1 & 0 \\ - 2021i & 1\end{cases}$\right]

$$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given equation is

\left|adj\left(adj\left(adj . A\right)\right)\right| = {12}^{4}$

$⇒ \left|A\right|( n - 1{)}^{3} = {12}^{4}$

$∵ n = 3$

$⇒ \left|A\right|( 3 - 1{)}^{3} = {12}^{4}$

$⇒ \left|A\right|8 = {12}^{4}$

$⇒ \left|A\right|2 = 12$

$⇒ \left|A\right| = 2\sqrt{3}$

Now,~\left|A^{- 1}adjA\right| = \left|A^{- 1}\right| . \left|adjA\right| = 1\left|A\right| \times \left|A\right|3 - 1$

$= \left|A\right| = 2\sqrt{3}$

questions.q: The total number of matrices $A = \left($\begin{cases}0 & 2y & 1 \\ 2x & y & - 1 \\ 2x & - y & 1\end{cases}$\right),  \left(x, y \in \mathbb{R}, x \ne y\right)$ for which $A^{T}A = 3{I}_{3} is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $A^{T}A = 3{I}_{3}$

\left($\begin{cases}0 & 2x & 2x \\ 2y & y & - y \\ 1 & - 1 & 1\end{cases}$\right)\left($\begin{cases}0 & 2y & 1 \\ 2x & y & - 1 \\ 2x & - y & 1\end{cases}$\right) = \left($\begin{cases}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{cases}$\right)$

\left($\begin{cases}8x^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 6y^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{cases}$\right) = \left($\begin{cases}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{cases}$\right)$

On comparing the two matrices, we get

$8x^{2} = 3$~and~$6y^{2} = 3$

$⇒ x^{2} = \dfrac{3}{8}$~and~$y^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ x = \pm \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{8}}$~and~$y = \pm \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

For each of~$x \text{ and } y$~we have two possible values, hence there are total~$2 \times 2 = 4$~combinations of values are possible.

Hence, total~$4$ matrices are possible.

questions.q: Let $A$ be a square matrix such that ${AA}^{T} = I$. Then $\dfrac{1}{2}A \left[  \left($A + A^{T}\right)2 + \left($A - A^{T}\right)2\right] is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: ${AA}^{T} = 1$

$⇒ A^{T} = A^{- 1}$

Now, solving

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}A\left[\left(A + A^{T}\right)2 + \left(A - A^{T}\right)2\right] = \dfrac{1}{2}A \times \left[2A^{2} + 2\left(A^{T}\right)2 + 2{AA}^{T} - 2{AA}^{T}\right]⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}A\left[\left(A + A^{T}\right)2 + \left(A - A^{T}\right)2\right] = $\dfrac{1}{2}$A \$times2\left[$A^{2} + \left($A^{T}\right)2\right]$

$⇒ $\ddfrac{1}{2}A\left[\left(A + A^{T}\right)2 + \left(A - A^{T}\right)2\right] = A^{3} + A\left(A^{T}\right)2$

Now using, ${AA}^{T} = 1$,

$⇒ $\d$dfrac{1}{2}A\left[\left($A + A^{T}\right)2 + \left($A - A^{T}\right)2\right] = A^{3} + A^{T}$

$

questions.q: Let $A$ be a $2 \times 2$~matrix with real entries such that $A^{'} = \alphaA + 1,$~ where $\alpha \in \mathbb{R} - \left\{- 1, 1\right\}$., If det \left(A^{2} - A\right) = 4$, the sum of all possible values of $\alpha$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$A$ be a $2 \times 2$~matrix with real entries such that $A^{'} = \alphaA + 1,$

Now let $A = \left[$\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}$\right]$

Now putting the value in~$A^{'} = \alphaA + I$~we get,

$⇒ \left[$\begin{cases}a & c \\ b & d\end{cases}$\right] = \left[$\begin{cases}\alphaa + 1 & \alphab \\ \alphac & \alphad + 1\end{cases}$\right]$

Now equating both side we get,

$a = \alphaa + 1 ⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{1 - \alpha} . . . . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

$b = \alphac . . . . \left(ii\right)$~and~$c = \alphab . . . . . . . . \left(iii\right)$

Now from equation \left($ii\right) \text{ and } \left(iii\right)$~we get,

$c = 0$~or $\alpha = \pm1$~(not possible as mentioned in question)

$∴ c = 0$

$⇒ c = 0, b = 0$
Also $d = \alphad + 1 ⇒ d = $\dfrac{1}{1 - \alpha}

Also given,~\left|A^{2} - A\right| = 4$

$⇒ | A | | A - I | = 4$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{1}{1 - \alpha}\rright)2\left(\dfrac{1}{1 - \alpha} -1\right)2 = 4$

Now let~$\dfrac{1}{1 - \alpha} =t$

So,~t^{2}\left($t - 1\right)2 = 4$

$⇒ $t\left($t - 1\right) = $\pm$2$

$⇒ t = $2\text{or}$t = - 1$

$⇒ $\alpha = $\dfrac{1}{2},2$

So, sum of all possible value will be~$\dfrac{1}{2} +2 = \dfrac{5}{2}$

$

questions.q: Let $S$~be the set containing all $3 \times 3$~matrices with entries from \left\{- 1, 0, 1\right\}$. The total number of matrices $A \in S$~such that the sum of all the diagonal elements of $A^{T}A$~is $6$ \text{ and } is ______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given that the sum of all the diagonal elements of $A^{T}A$~is $6$, means sum of all diagonal elements is equal to sum of square each element of the matrix.

i.e.,~$A = \left[$\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {a}_{2} & {a}_{3} \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & {b}_{3} \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}$\right]$~and~$A^{T} = \left[$\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}$\right]$

Then~${t}_{r}\left(A \cdot A^{T}\right)= {a}_{1}^{2} + {a}_{2}^{2} + {a}_{3}^{2} + {b}_{1}^{2} + {b}_{2}^{2} + {b}_{3}^{2} + {c}_{1}^{2} + {c}_{2}^{2} + {c}_{3}^{2}$

Given~${a}_{i}, {b}_{i}, {c}_{i} \in \left\{- 1, 0, 1\right\}$~for~$i = 1, 2, 3$

Now sum to be $6$~exactly three of them should be~zero and rest should be~$1$~or~$- 1$.

So, total number~of possible matrices~$C3 9 \times {2}^{6}$

$= \dfrac{9 \times 8 \times 7}{6} \times 64$

$= 5376$

questions.q: Let $A = \left[$\begin{cases}x & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{cases}$\right], xεR$ and $A^{4} = \left[{a}_{ij}\right] .$ If ${a}_{11} = 109,$ then ${a}_{22}$ is equal to_____________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$A^{2} = \left[$\begin{cases}x & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{cases}$\right] \times \left[$\begin{cases}x & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{cases}$\right] = \left[$\begin{cases}x^{2} + 1 & x \\ x & 1\end{cases}$\right]$

$A^{4} = \left[$\begin{cases}x^{2} + 1 & x \\ x & 1\end{cases}$\right] \times \left[$\begin{cases}x^{2} + 1 & x \\ x & 1\end{cases}$\right] = \left[$\begin{cases}x^{4} + 3x^{2} + 1 & x^{3} + 2x \\ x^{3} + 2x & x^{2} + 1\end{cases}$\right]$

Given~${a}_{11} = 109 ⇒ x^{4} + 3x^{2} + 1 = 109$

\left(x^{2} + 12\right)\left(x^{2} - 9\right) = 0 ⇒ x^{2} = 9$

$∴ {a}_{22} = x^{2} + 1 = 10$

$
